data.narrative:
SatSure, a Series B frontier-tech company in Space & Aerospace founded by Prateep Basu, is evaluated against a peer universe of 5 private and 6 public comparables in the same sector. The private peer set includes Sierra Space, Cowboy Space Corporation, Varda Space Industries, Aalyria, and Skyryse; the public anchors span Rocket Lab (RKLB), Planet Labs (PL), Lunar Resources (LUNR), AST SpaceMobile (ASTS), and Satellite Labs (SATL).

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. The median valuation across the 5 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private peers is $1.5B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Skyryse, Series C) to $8.0B (Sierra Space, Series C). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples cannot be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue; the Space & Aerospace sector median P/S across public comparables is 23.9x, but this requires target-level revenue data unavailable for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B to $1.7B, with a median of $1.5B. This range reflects peer positioning but carries meaningful uncertainty around SatSure's business-specific traction metrics, revenue trajectory, and operational progress relative to the public and private benchmark set. The wide dispersion in peer valuations ($1.1B–$8.0B) underscores stage-dependent variance and company-specific risk factors not captured in median-based estimates.
